questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(A) The dog barked loudly at the stranger, / (B) standing protective / (C) in front of its owner / (D) and alerting everyone in the vicinity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary issue lies in part **(B)** of the sentence: "standing protective."
 
• The phrase "standing protective" is grammatically incorrect. It should be corrected to "standing protectively" to properly use the adverb "protectively" instead of the adjective "protective."
 
• Adverbs are used to modify verbs, and here "standing" requires the adverb "protectively" to describe the manner in which the action is performed.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The dog barked loudly at the stranger, standing protectively in front of its owner and alerting everyone in the vicinity."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence.

She was feeling **under the weather**, so she decided to go to bed in order to sleep.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Hit the sack**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Under the weather"** means feeling unwell or slightly ill. (बीमार महसूस करना)

 
 
• **Example:** He has been feeling under the weather since yesterday, so he decided to rest at home.
 
 
 
• **"Hit the sack"** refers to going to bed to sleep. (सोने जाना)
 
 
• **Example:** After a long day at work, she was so tired that she decided to hit the sack early.
 
 
 
• In this context, the highlighted phrase "under the weather" suggests that she was not feeling well, so the correct idiom to describe her action of going to bed is "hit the sack."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Bark up the wrong tree** (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना): To pursue a mistaken or misguided course of action.

 
 
• **Example:** If you think I took your book, you're barking up the wrong tree.
 
 
 
• **Cry over spilled milk** (बीती बातों पर पछताना): To waste time worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be changed.
 
 
• **Example:** There's no use crying over spilled milk; we need to move on and find a solution.
 
 
 
• **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): A way of wishing someone good luck, especially before a performance.
 
 
• **Example:** You're going to do great in the play tonight! Break a leg!

• The other options: "**sounding**," "**loud**," and "**cracking**" do not convey the same meaning or fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Despite initial problems, the plan has been a roaring__ success.*

• **Loud**: refers to something that produces a strong sound, but it does not appropriately describe success.
 
• **Cracking**: typically means excellent or very good, but it is less commonly used in this context compared to "roaring success."

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

On the occasion of Teacher's Day, / the students of the community school / light applauded the performance / of the teachers.

options.text: the students of the community school
On the occasion of Teacher's Day,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The issue lies in the usage of the word "**light applauded**" in Option 3.
 
• The adverb "**light**" is incorrectly used here. The correct adverb should be "**lightly**" to modify the verb "**applauded**" appropriately.
 
• Adverbs are used to describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, and they often end in "-ly."
 
• Thus, the phrase should be "**lightly applauded the performance**" for grammatical correctness.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"On the occasion of Teacher's Day, the students of the community school lightly applauded the performance of the teachers."*
